long_biography.plain_text:
Taking Sonic's chair after his father's death placed David Bruton Smith at the centre of a family-business succession. He had become chief executive four years earlier and had served in the organisation since 1998. The change combined board leadership with authority over the retailer his father founded and positioned Smith to continue a strategy already focused on national growth.

His most consequential expansion as chief executive was the acquisition of RFJ Auto Partners. The transaction added 33 locations across seven states and broadened Sonic's brand portfolio. Smith also backed a company-wide minimum hourly wage for Sonic and EchoPark employees, arguing that workforce investment should accompany stronger performance. The policy placed employee retention alongside acquisitions and technology in the retailer's operating programme.

uncertainties.detail: David Bruton Smith is living and remains Sonic's chairman and chief executive in 2026. His father, founder O. Bruton Smith, died in June 2022. The dossier does not transfer the founder title, mortality or motorsports achievements from father to son.

Current SEC filings establish David's direct interests and shared control through family entities, while official records establish the founder-father relationship and David's subsequent expansion work. They do not itemise which holdings arose through inheritance, earlier family transfer or executive compensation, limiting origin confidence to 90.

The 2026 proxy reports Smith as age 51 but does not provide a birth date. Age alone does not establish a unique birth year at the required confidence, so birth day, month, year and birthplace remain unproposed.

The immutable record already contains LinkedIn and Instagram URLs, so they are not re-proposed. Automated access to both profiles was restricted, no strong official cross-link to a personal website was found, and no additional personal social cleared the verification threshold.
No dedicated Forbes profile for David Bruton Smith was found. Forbes reporting on motorsports and the wider Smith family does not establish a personal profile URL.

Current revenue, quarterly results, share prices, rankings, executive compensation, private-family information, politics, legal matters, allegations, controversy and vessel material are excluded from both biographies.
